headline: Witkoff and Kushner Reach Kyiv After Moscow Talks
deck: The U.S. envoys' first Kyiv visit moved the peace push from Putin's table to Zelenskyy's, with the travel route and ceasefire language still disputed.
body: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for their first visit to Ukraine as Trump envoys, turning a weekend shuttle into an open sequence rather than a rumored channel. Zelenskyy posted that talks had begun after greeting them in the capital, and Reuters reported that British, French and German national security advisers were also in Kyiv. The order now on the record is Moscow first, Poland overnight, then Zelenskyy's table, before any public terms exist. [E1] [E3]

Kyiv set its public position before the meeting rather than after it. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had prepared its proposals, wanted an end to the war, security guarantees and what he called a dignified peace; the Kremlin's prior readout from Moscow instead emphasized Russia's account of the war's root causes. Those are positions around a table, not proof that a draft settlement has been put on one. [E2] [E7]

Route into Kyiv became part of the story because the Americans did not land there. CNN reported the U.S. aircraft came into Rzeszow in Poland and that the envoys continued by rail; Zelenskyy said Ukraine had readied airports but Russian strikes showed the visitors could not land or use an aircraft. That second point is Kyiv's attribution, not a Washington-confirmed causal finding. The alternative reading is that U.S. security planners would have chosen the rail leg regardless; the plain fact that would settle it is a U.S. movement order or airport damage assessment tying the route to those strikes. [E4] [E6]

Public images established the arrival gate that was missing earlier in the day. The Guardian described the Sophia Square greeting, while Zelenskyy's own post moved the visit from expectation to talks underway. That matters because the pair had already met Putin in Moscow, so the live development was not simply another envoy trip but the first visible Ukrainian stop after that session. [E5] [E1]

Ceasefire language remained deliberately narrow in the research record. Ukraine's offer was a pause on strikes against Moscow through Monday, while Russia's stated order covered Kyiv for three days; the Kremlin transcript said Putin had not accepted Ukraine's broader three-day truce. Calling that a ceasefire would add a scope neither side has established. [E7] [E3]

European presence was the least settled piece of the day's sequence. Reuters had it from a source that the British, French and German national security advisers were also in Kyiv, but the record here does not show whether they joined Zelenskyy's meeting or worked a parallel track. If they entered the same room, the relay starts to look like a contact-group conversation; if they did not, the hard fact remains a U.S. meeting with Kyiv after Moscow. [E3]

By Sunday afternoon, the verified sequence was narrower than the claims attached to it. The U.S. envoys were in Kyiv, Zelenskyy said talks had begun, the trip followed the Kremlin session, and the route ran through Poland by rail. What still lacked proof was the content of any proposal and the U.S. government's own account of why the envoys did not fly directly into Ukraine. [E1] [E4]
key_numbers: 1 first Kyiv visit by Witkoff and Kushner as Trump envoys
3 days in Russia's stated no-strikes order for Kyiv

evidence_box.fragment: Zelenskyy said talks with the U.S. envoys had begun after their arrival in Kyiv.
Before the Kyiv greeting, Zelenskyy posted Ukraine's public ask: prepared proposals, an end to the war, security guarantees and a dignified peace after the war.

Reuters reported that Witkoff and Kushner made their first Kyiv visit as Trump envoys after the Kremlin session, began talks with Zelenskyy, and that British, French and German national security advisers were also in Kyiv, citing a source.
CNN reported the U.S. aircraft came into Rzeszow in Poland and that Witkoff and Kushner continued toward Kyiv by rail.
The Guardian described the Sophia Square greeting in Kyiv after the U.S. envoys arrived for talks on ending the war.

evidence_box.source: Ukrainska Pravda / hromadske on the aircraft claim
evidence_box.fragment: Zelenskyy said Russian strikes showed the envoys could not land or use an aircraft in Ukraine.

evidence_box.source: special.kremlin.ru - Kremlin 5 Sep transcript (pause scope, root causes)
evidence_box.fragment: The Kremlin transcript says Putin gave the U.S. envoys Russia's account of the conflict's root causes, described Russia's no-strikes order for Kyiv, and said he had not agreed to Ukraine's broader three-day truce proposal.
